title: How to compare online brokerages for beginners in the US
description: A framework for evaluating Fidelity, Schwab, and Robinhood beyond just 'Zero Commissions'.
content:
In 2025, almost every US brokerage offers $0 stock trades. The price war is over; the feature war has begun. For a beginner, choosing between Fidelity, Charles Schwab, Robinhood, or Vanguard can be overwhelming. They all 'do' the same thing (buy stocks), but their user experience, hidden fees, and auxiliary features differ wildly. Choosing the wrong platform can mean lower interest on your cash, clunky interfaces that discourage investing, or temptation to gamble. This guide provides a scorecard for picking your financial home.

Key Takeaways

  • The 'Cash Sweep' Metric: This is the biggest differentiator in 2025. Fidelity pays ~5% on uninvested cash automatically. Schwab pays ~0.4%. On $10k cash, that's a $460/year difference.
  • Fractional Shares: Essential for beginners. Fidelity allows fractional buys of everything (Stocks/ETFs). Schwab only allows S&P 500 stocks. Vanguard allows almost none.
  • Interface vs. Information: Robinhood wins on UX (ease of use). Schwab wins on Research (data). Fidelity is the middle ground.
  • Customer Service: When you get locked out, who picks up the phone? The legacy brokers (Fidelity/Schwab) have 24/7 support. Apps often use chatbots.

Why It Matters (US Context)

SIPC Insurance ($500k protection) is standard across all major US brokers. The safety of your assets is generally equal. The difference is in the tools, the interest rates, and the 'nudge' architecture (do they push you to trade or hold?).

The Brokerage Scorecard

Rate the platforms based on your specific needs.

1. Fidelity (The All-Rounder)

  • Cash Sweep: Auto-sweeps to SPAXX (~5%). Winner.
  • Fractional Shares: Stocks and ETFs. Winner.
  • Fees: $0. No pattern day trade fees.
  • Verdict: The best default choice for 90% of investors.

2. Charles Schwab (The Traveler/Trader)

  • Cash Sweep: Poor (~0.4%). You must manually buy SWVXX to get yield.
  • Banking: Investor Checking refunds ALL ATM fees globally. Winner.
  • Research: Thinkorswim platform is pro-level.
  • Verdict: Best for banking integration and advanced traders.

3. Robinhood (The UX King)

  • Cash Sweep: 5% (only with Gold subscription, $5/mo).
  • IRA Match: 1-3% match on contributions. Winner.
  • Interface: Beautiful, simple, fast.
  • Verdict: Best for taxable accounts and Roth IRAs if you can resist the urge to gamble on options.

How to Decide

  1. The 'Sit Test': Download the apps. Which one makes sense to your brain? If you find the app confusing, you won't use it. UX matters.
  2. The IRA Factor: If opening an IRA, Robinhood's match is mathematically superior (free money). If opening a heavy cash account, Fidelity wins.
  3. The 'One Login' Rule: Do you already have a 401(k) at Fidelity? Keep your IRA there too. Simplicity prevents mistakes.
  4. Avoid: Banks (Chase/Wells). Their brokerage platforms are often clunky and they might charge hidden fees. Stick to dedicated brokerages.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is it hard to switch?

No. The ACATS system automates it. You open the new account and click 'Transfer Assets'. It pulls them over in 5-7 days. Note: The old broker might charge $75, but the new one usually reimburses it.

What is Payment for Order Flow (PFOF)?

It's how 'Free' brokers make money. They sell your trade to a market maker. You might get a price of $100.01 instead of $100.00. For long-term investors, this penny cost is irrelevant compared to the $0 commission.

Can I use Vanguard directly?

You can, but their app is widely considered outdated. You can buy Vanguard ETFs (VTI) inside Fidelity or Robinhood for free, getting the best funds with a better app.
